summary: Describes how to use the GSS-API naming extensions to access authorization and personalization attributes carried by the EAP GSS-API mechanism, including attributes from AAA responses and SAML messages. This lets applications make authorization decisions using that information.

plainLanguage.summary: After you sign in, the system holds notes about you. This explains how programs can read those notes.

questions: how to read saml attributes from gss-eap
subtitle: How applications read RADIUS and SAML attributes about an authenticated user through GSS-API name attributes.

tldr.problem: The GSS-API EAP mechanism can carry authorization data and SAML assertions from an AAA server, but applications need standard names to find that data.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7056 defines URN-based attribute names for RADIUS attributes, SAML assertions, SAML attributes and SAML name identifiers, to be used with the GSS-API naming extensions.
tldr.outcome: Applications can read authenticated attributes about a user after authentication, but must still decide whether the identity provider is trusted to assert each one.

today: RFC 7056 is a Proposed Standard, published in December 2013, and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on RFC 7055.

sections.title: Purpose of the Name Attributes
sections.content:
The GSS-API naming extensions (RFC 6680) let applications discover authorization and personalization information associated with a GSS-API name. The Extensible Authentication Protocol GSS-API mechanism (RFC 7055) lets an Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) peer send authorization attributes alongside an authentication response. It also processes SAML messages carried in that response.

RFC 7056 describes how to use the naming extensions API to reach that information. Other mechanisms, such as SAML Enhanced Client, can also carry SAML assertions and attributes in GSS-API.

The semantics of setting these attributes are undefined and left to future work.
sections.plainLanguage: When you log in, extra facts about you travel along. This RFC explains how a program can look those facts up by name.

sections.title: How SAML Attributes Get Their Names
sections.content:
A SAML attribute name has two parts: a URI describing the format of the name, and the name itself. GSS-API attributes carrying SAML data have three parts: a URN stating that it is a SAML attribute and giving its context, then a space, the format URI, a space, and the SAML attribute name. The format URI is not optional and MUST be present.

SAML attribute names may not be globally unique, because two issuers can pick the same name for different meanings. Attributes in the federated context are issued by the same party that performs the authentication, so the meaning can be worked out from who the subject is.
sections.plainLanguage: Every label has the kind of label it is, then the actual name, so two schools using the same word cannot be mixed up.

sections.title: The Federated Context and Trust
sections.content:
An authenticated name attribute is one that the mechanism guarantees to be an authenticated statement from the trusted source of the peer credential. That does not mean the source is authorized to assert it.

In a federation, the trusted source is typically an identity provider. In GSS-EAP the SAML Identity Provider and the home AAA server are assumed to be in the same trust domain, which usually differs from the service's own. An academic federation might trust an identity provider's claim that someone is a student or professor, but not its claim about local entitlements such as group membership.

So a service MUST make a policy decision about whether the identity provider may assert a particular attribute and whether the value is acceptable. That policy can be local configuration, rules in AAA proxies or other deployment-specific mechanisms. In contrast, an enterprise setting such as Kerberos typically has a central infrastructure trusted for most attributes.

The federated-context names MUST NOT be used for attributes from a party other than one closely associated with the source of credentials, unless that source is re-asserting them.
sections.plainLanguage: A school can say you are a student, but it should not get to say you are allowed into the gym at another school. The program checking has to decide what to believe.

sections.title: RADIUS Attribute Names
sections.content:
RADIUS attributes received in an access-accept message by the GSS-EAP mechanism are named with urn:ietf:params:gss:radius-attribute, a space, and a numeric RADIUS name as described in RFC 6929. For example, User-Name is urn:ietf:params:gss:radius-attribute 1, and extended type 1 within type 241 is urn:ietf:params:gss:radius-attribute 241.1.

These meanings apply to the src_name output of GSS_Accept_sec_context after it returns GSS_S_COMPLETE. Use for other RADIUS messages, or before the access-accept, is undefined.

To read the username, an application waits for GSS_S_COMPLETE, calls GSS_Get_name_attribute with that name and the attribute string, confirms the authenticated output is true, and reads the values output.

Values are the raw octets of the packet, with integers in network byte order. The display value SHOULD be human-readable if the type is known. Multiple attributes with one name SHOULD give a multi-valued GSS-API attribute, except that attributes split across several RADIUS attributes to carry more than 253 octets SHOULD be concatenated.
sections.plainLanguage: Each fact the login server sends has a number. To find the username, you ask for fact number 1 after the login has finished.

sections.title: SAML Assertion, Attribute and Name ID Names
sections.content:
Three kinds of SAML data get names. The whole assertion is urn:ietf:params:gss:federated-saml-assertion. It is absent if no assertion is present or it fails local policy checks, and it is marked authenticated only if the mechanism can authenticate the SAML statement. For GSS-EAP that is true once the AAA exchange has authenticated. Applications MUST confirm the authenticated flag, because other mechanisms MAY allow an unauthenticated statement.

Each attribute in the assertion SHOULD be a name attribute with three parts separated by ASCII spaces: urn:ietf:params:gss:federated-saml-attribute, the URI for the NameFormat, and the attribute Name. Spaces inside a URI are encoded as %20. If the value is simple text, the raw and display values MUST be that text, encoded as UTF-8. Otherwise the raw value MUST be a namespace well-formed serialization of the <saml:AttributeValue> elements in UTF-8, and the display value is implementation defined.

The <saml:NameID> SHOULD be named urn:ietf:params:gss:federated-saml-nameid plus a space and the Format URI. Its raw value MUST be the serialized element in UTF-8, with the defaulting rules for the "persistent" and "transient" formats applied first.

These SHOULD be marked authenticated when the assertion is validated back to the trusted source. In GSS-EAP, an assertion carried in an integrity-protected, authenticated AAA protocol SHALL be treated as validated. Implementations MAY discard any item that fails local policy checks.
sections.plainLanguage: The whole signed note, each fact inside it, and the name of the person on it each get their own label. A program asks for the label it wants.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
These attributes serve two purposes. The less sensitive is personalization, where a central service supplies details so users need not retype them at each acceptor. The more sensitive is authorization.

The mechanism handles authentication and integrity protection. The acceptor application decides whether the credential source is trusted to assert the attribute and validates the value. Because mechanisms may apply local policy checks, an application reaching the same SAML by another route, such as the mechanism in AAA-SAML, can see different results. This is intended, and applications that bypass the checks SHOULD do their own evaluation.

IANA created a "Generic Security Service Application Program Interface Parameters" registry with a "GSS-API URN Parameters" subregistry (IETF Review or Expert Review), and registered the "gss" URN sub-namespace.
sections.plainLanguage: The login system promises the notes were not changed on the way. The program using them still has to decide whether to believe each note.

viz.caption: ATTRIBUTE NAME PREFIXES REGISTERED BY RFC 7056

messages.label: authenticated + values
messages.note: Check that authenticated is true, then read the username.
